newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index firms on gains to VSZ shares.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index firms on gains to VSZ shares.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed on low volumes on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with gains to steel producer VSZ boosting the 16-share SAX index 0.84 points to 194.54.
VSZ, which closed up 10 crowns at 740 on a volume of 10,038 shares, has been the only blue chip of late to show signs of life, while other shares remained illiquid, brokers said.
"There is constant interest in VSZ, which makes it a bright exception on this sickly market at the moment," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said. "It can rise further."

He said that the VSZ gains were probably not caused by Thursday's changes to the company's supervisory board, including appointment of former transport minister Alexander Rezes a chairman of the board.
"Everybody (on market) was expecting that," Briska said.

Shares of oil refinery Slovnaft weakened five crowns to 995, after the company posted lower 1996 profits of 1.3 billion rowns, down from 1.8 billion the previous year as costs from rising crude oil prices and general maintenace bit into the firm's bottom line.

But dealers said the issue remained attractive. "It's still a good stock, only suffering from a lack of liquidity as there is nobody at the moment willing to buy it," Briska said. Only 30 shares of Slovnaft traded on the BSE floor.
Overall volume eased to 506,266 shares, from 551,648 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover decreased to 401.01 million crowns, from 588.37 million.
